Goodwin Generated Mission America Explained

What it takes to run 50 states.

A fast, plain-English guide to the food, recovery, travel, equipment, purpose, and donation questions behind Goodwin Generated Mission America.

50Marathons
24Days
1Mission
The Basics

Goodwin Generated Mission America is simple to say and difficult to execute.

William Goodge is attempting one marathon in every U.S. state inside a compressed 24-day window. The running is only one layer. The project also depends on nutrition, sleep, bodywork, live tracking, media, community participation, and Goodwin's travel operation.

01
The Athlete

Who is Will Goodge?

Goodge, known by some as the fastest man to run across Australia, crossed the country on foot in just over 35 days (2,361 miles). He has also run from Los Angeles to New York in 55 days (3,011 miles), and spent the last decade engineering a body and mind capable of what most consider biologically impossible.

He runs in memory of his mother, Amanda, who died of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma in 2018. Every project he takes on is a fundraiser. Every mile is a tribute.

02
The Partnership

Why is Goodwin involved?

Goodwin Generated Mission America is the first chapter of the Goodwin Endurance Series — an ultra-endurance platform built around athletes attempting things history hasn't seen yet.

The Goodwin Company backs people willing to push beyond what most consider possible. William Goodge was chosen to kick off the series because he doesn't talk about limits. He runs through them.

Mission America brings those two ideas together: an athlete built for extreme endurance and a company built to solve the operational challenges required to make an attempt of this scale possible.

03
The Origin

How did this all come together?

The Founder of Goodwin and Will Goodge went on a run and talked about what challenge Will was looking to take on next. Will's dream was to set a world record by running 50 marathons in 50 states in the quickest time ever. Goodwin's Founder joked that he had access to "time machines" — airplanes — and a dream started to turn into a plan.

04
Run With Will

Can anyone join?

Every run will have an option for outside participants to join in this historic achievement by running the first 5K of the marathon with Will. Since he is running in every state, there is a good chance he will be running close to you, and this is the perfect time to be part of a world record and run with William Goodge.

Whether you want to sign up as an entire run club or as an individual, use the Run With Will signup to register your interest.

05
Recovery

Where does Will eat and sleep?

Goodge will be eating and sleeping on the go — in the RV and wherever the schedule allows. Team members are providing nutrition and hydration protocols for every run, along with a regimented rest and sleep schedule.

06
Logistics

How is travel between states handled?

Goodwin Generated Mission America runs on precision. The Goodwin Company provides the aerial transport, support fleet, and operational intelligence that make 50 marathons in 24 days physically possible.

The same exacting standards Goodwin applies to flight are applied to human performance. The Goodwin Company coordinates the entire route, including private-aviation rotations, commercial airlines, and RV transfers.

07
Food

What does Will eat?

Simple, repeatable fuel wins: carbohydrates in motion, fast protein after, electrolytes everywhere, and meals chosen for performance over novelty.

The goal is not culinary variety. It is predictable energy, easy digestion, and a system the crew can repeat under time pressure.

08
Training

How does he prepare?

The block is built around durable aerobic volume, back-to-back long efforts, strength maintenance, and recovery rehearsed under travel pressure.

The hard part is not one marathon. It is resetting fast enough to make tomorrow's marathon possible.

09
Recovery

What happens between runs?

Each transfer is engineered: rehydrate, refuel, reset the body, protect sleep, prepare the kit, and move cleanly to the next start line.

Recovery becomes part of the route plan, not something that happens after the work is done.

10
Travel

How does Will travel between race sites?

Goodwin coordinates the movement between stops with the same open-book precision behind the route map: aviation, ground transfers, timing, and recovery windows working together.

Every handoff has to protect the next run.
11
Equipment

What equipment does Will use?

The kit stays simple and proven: rotating shoes, reliable run apparel, hydration, nutrition, recovery tools, and tracking gear that can hold up to daily marathon mileage.

12
Sleep

How does Will sleep?

Sleep is treated as part of the performance system. The team protects quiet windows, manages travel timing, and keeps recovery repeatable from one city to the next.

The Crew

Giving

How can I donate?

The final donation destination is not live yet. For now, point supporters to the Goodwin Generated Mission America donation site; we can update this link once the permanent public URL is confirmed.

15
Purpose

What is Will running for?

Will runs in memory of his mother, Amanda, and in support of everyone fighting cancer. Goodwin Generated Mission America turns the endurance challenge into a public platform for awareness, fundraising, and community participation.

The mileage matters because the mission matters.

Goodwin Company builds next-generation infrastructure for charter aviation and backs athletes redefining human endurance.
